id: 评分者一致性cohens-kappa-置信区间精度估计
previous_headings: 第六章：复杂与现代前沿临床研究设计
what: 6.8 评分者一致性：Cohen’s Kappa 置信区间精度估计
title: SampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 研究背景与人群：两位放射科医生拟在一套预先构建、阳性与阴性判读比例接近平衡的乳腺影像评估样本中，估计二分类判读的一致性。 实施与主要结局：两位医生相互盲法独立判读同一批影像，每名患者形成一对分类结果；κ 描述超出偶然一致的一致程度，不是敏感度或特异度。 参数设定与依据：本例使用平衡边际比例 pi1 = pi2 = 0.50、预期 kappa = 0.70、95% 区间半宽 d = 0.10。正式研究的边际比例应来自拟应用人群或明确的样本富集方案。 设计选择：这是单个 κ 的精度规划，分析单位是被判读的患者/标本。读者人数固定为两名，增加同一图像的重复判读不能替代更多独立标本。 数学公式与出处： \[n = Q\left(\frac{z_{1-\alpha/2}}{d}\right)^2, \quad Q = \frac{p_o(1-p_o)}{(1-p_e)^2}\] 出处：Cantor, . B. (1996). Psychol Methods, 1(2), 150-153. 输出解读与招募安排：需 196 个独立标本，每个由两位读者各判读一次，共 392 次判读。这一结果对应本例的平衡判读样本，不能把同一精度要求直接套用于边际比例明显不同的人群。
code: res_6_8 <- calculate("kappa", "estimate", "proportion", pi1 = 0.50, pi2 = 0.50, kappa = 0.70, d = 0.10, alpha = 0.05) print(res_6_8) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Cohen's kappa estimation (CI precision)" #> • Required sample size: 196 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • pi1/pi2 = expected Rating-1 proportions for rater 1 / rater 2 #> • kappa1 = planning value of kappa #> • d = desired CI half-width #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = Q * (z/d)^2; Q is the full asymptotic variance factor from Cantor (1996), #> Eq 3` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = Q\left(\frac{z_{1-\alpha/2}}{d}\right)^2, \quad Q = n\operatorname{Var}(\widehat{\kappa})\;\text{(Cantor Eq. 3)}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Identify study design: Cohen's kappa estimation (CI precision). #> • Step 2: Input parameters: pi1 = 0.50, pi2 = 0.50, kappa = 0.70, d = 0.10, #> alpha = 0.05, Q = 0.51. #> • Step 3: Apply design formula: n = Q * (z/d)^2; Q is the full asymptotic #> variance factor from Cantor (1996), Eq 3. #> • Step 4: Calculated sample size metrics: Required sample size: 196; Total #> sample size: 196. #> Reference: #> Primary: Cantor, A. B. (1996). Sample-size calculations for Cohen's kappa. Psychological Methods, 1(2), 150-153 (Fleiss-Cohen-Everitt 1969 asymptotic variance; worked examples N=165 and N=214). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

id: 评分者一致性两独立-kappa-系数差异检验
previous_headings: 第六章：复杂与现代前沿临床研究设计
what: 6.9 评分者一致性：两独立 Kappa 系数差异检验
title: SampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 研究背景与人群：影像科拟比较结构化报告清单与常规判读流程的一致性，将两组独立的患者影像分别用于两种流程，每个组内由两位读者形成配对判读。 实施与主要结局：分别估计两组 κ，再比较其差异；两组标本来源与疾病谱应可比。相同影像被两种流程重复判读时，两个 κ 不再独立，不能直接套用本例。 参数设定与依据：设 κ 为 0.70 与 0.50，边际比例均为 0.50，双侧 α=0.05、效能 80%。所需人数指每组被判读的标本数，不是需要招募同样数量的放射科医生。 设计选择：采用两个独立 κ 的差异检验，读者培训和阳性判定标准需保持可比，避免流程间系统性地改变分类定义。 数学公式与出处： \[n = \frac{\left[z_{\alpha}\sqrt{2Q_1} + z_{\beta}\sqrt{Q_1+Q_2}\right]^2}{(K_1-K_2)^2}\] 出处：Cantor, . B. (1996). Psychol Methods, 1(2), 150-153. 输出解读与执行安排：每组需 214 个标本，两组合计 428 个；每个标本由两位读者评价，因此合计约 856 次判读。
code: res_6_9 <- calculate("kappa", "test", "proportion", pi1 = 0.50, pi2 = 0.50, kappa1 = 0.70, kappa2 = 0.50, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_6_9) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Cohen's kappa test (two independent kappas)" #> • Required sample size: 214 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • pi1/pi2 = expected Rating-1 proportions (both raters/groups) #> • kappa1 = kappa under the null (e.g. questionnaire 1) #> • kappa2 = kappa under the alternative (e.g. questionnaire 2) #> • n is per group (two independent kappa estimates) #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = (z_a*sqrt(2*Q1) + z_b*sqrt(Q1+Q2))^2/(K1-K2)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{\left[z_{\alpha}\sqrt{2Q_1} + z_{\beta}\sqrt{Q_1+Q_2}\right]^2}{(K_1-K_2)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Identify study design: Cohen's kappa test (two independent kappas). #> • Step 2: Input parameters: pi1 = 0.50, pi2 = 0.50, kappa1 = 0.70, kappa2 = #> 0.50, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80, Q_null = 0.51, Q_alt = 0.75. #> • Step 3: Apply design formula: n = (z_a*sqrt(2*Q1) + #> z_b*sqrt(Q1+Q2))^2/(K1-K2)^2. #> • Step 4: Calculated sample size metrics: Required sample size: 214; Total #> sample size: 214. #> Reference: #> Primary: Cantor, A. B. (1996). Sample-size calculations for Cohen's kappa. Psychological Methods, 1(2), 150-153 (worked example: K1=0.7, K2=0.5, pi=0.5 -> N=214). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

previous_headings: 第六章：复杂与现代前沿临床研究设计
what: 6.10 中断时间序列研究（Interrupted Time Series, ITS）
title: SampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 研究背景与人群：医院拟在明确的日期实施抗菌药管理政策，利用实施前 12 个月和实施后 12 个月的月度抗菌药使用强度监测其即时水平变化。 实施与主要结局：每个时间点为全院月度汇总指标，例如每百住院患者日的用药强度；时间点之间可能相关，月内患者数不是本计算的独立样本量。 参数设定与依据：设即时变化为结局残差 SD 的 2 倍，即 effect_sd = 2，AR(1) 相关系数 rho = 0.30，n_pre = n_post = 12。该标准化效应是较强的演示假设，不能读成下降 2%。 设计选择：给定时间点数后计算近似效能，仅描述水平跃变及简化 AR(1) 调整。季节性、原有趋势、渐进斜率变化或同时发生的其他政策，需要在正式分段回归或模拟中处理。 数学公式与出处： \[\text{power} = \Phi\left(\frac{\delta}{SE} - z_{\alpha/2}\right), \quad SE = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{n_{eff}^{pre}} + \tfrac{1}{n_{eff}^{post}}}, \quad n_{eff} = \frac{n(1-\rho)}{1+\rho}\] 出处：Bernal et al. (2017). Int J Epidemiol, 46(1), 348-355（AR(1) 校正近似，试验性方法）。 输出解读与执行安排：24 个月度时间点在本近似下的效能为 94.9%。结果不表示需要 24 名患者，也不保证已充分控制季节与时间趋势；需结合预计月度数据质量安排监测长度和分析。
code: res_6_10 <- calculate("its", "test", "rate", effect_sd = 2, n_pre = 12, n_post = 12, rho = 0.3, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) print(res_6_10) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Interrupted time series (level change, AR(1)-adjusted)" #> • Power achieved: 0.949 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • effect_sd = anticipated level change in outcome SD units #> • n_pre/n_post = number of time points before/after the interruption #> • rho = AR(1) autocorrelation of the series #> ! EXPERIMENTAL method: transparent AR(1)-adjusted normal approximation. #> ! Bernal et al. (2017, Int J Epidemiol) recommend >= 8 time points per segment; #> ! rigorous ITS power calculations require simulation. #>  #> Formula (plain text): #> `power = Phi(effect/SE - z); SE = sqrt(1/n_eff_pre + 1/n_eff_post); n_eff = #> n(1-rho)/(1+rho)` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$\text{power} = \Phi\left(\frac{\delta}{SE} - z_{\alpha/2}\right), \quad SE = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{n_{eff}^{pre}} + \tfrac{1}{n_{eff}^{post}}}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Identify study design: Interrupted time series (level change, #> AR(1)-adjusted). #> • Step 2: Input parameters: effect_sd = 2, n_pre = 12, n_post = 12, rho = 0.30, #> alpha = 0.05. #> • Step 3: Apply design formula: power = Phi(effect/SE - z); SE = #> sqrt(1/n_eff_pre + 1/n_eff_post); n_eff = n(1-rho)/(1+rho). #> • Step 4: Calculated sample size metrics: Power achieved: 0.949. #> Reference: #> Framework: Bernal, J. L., Cummins, S., & Gasparrini, A. (2017). Interrupted time series regression for the evaluation of public health interventions: a tutorial. International Journal of Epidemiology, 46(1), 348-355. Sample-size content is a transparent approximation, not from a validated source. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

id: 方案-a降压-rct-的参数依据与预算敏感性
previous_headings: 第七章：结果解读、标书撰写模板与实战图表展示 > 两份完整方案如何落地
what: 方案 A：降压 RCT 的参数依据与预算敏感性
title: SampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 第 1.1 节的入组人群、12 周降幅终点、独立患者分析单位需要同时写进方案。参数依据应具体到研究编号、样本规模、降幅均值及 SD；若文献只报告基线血压或标准误，先完成适当转换或获取所需资料，再代入计算。 下表保留对照组均值 10、双侧 α=0.05、效能 80%，比较 SD 从 3 增至 4、真实组间差从 2 缩小至 1.5 的影响。每组招募数另按 10% 缺失膨胀，适合用于评估招募预算是否能覆盖合理的不确定性。 方案中应明确最终采用哪一行、原因是什么、能否按期获得这些独立患者及完整终点评估。不能以“所有参数都来自文献”为概括，省略不同研究人群和测量定义的差异。
code: rct_plan <- data.frame(   scenario = c("基准假设", "变异更大", "差异更小", "两项同时变化"),   mean2 = c(12, 12, 11.5, 11.5),   sd = c(3, 4, 3, 4) ) rct_plan$complete <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(rct_plan)), function(i) {   calculate("rct", "test", "mean",     mean1 = 10, mean2 = rct_plan$mean2[i], sd = rct_plan$sd[i]   )$n_per_group }, numeric(1)) rct_plan$recruit <- ceiling(rct_plan$complete / 0.9) knitr::kable(rct_plan,   col.names = c("情景", "研究组均值", "降幅 SD", "可分析人数/组", "招募人数/组") )

id: 方案-b敏感度研究的病例配额与筛查容量
previous_headings: 第七章：结果解读、标书撰写模板与实战图表展示 > 两份完整方案如何落地
what: 方案 B：敏感度研究的病例配额与筛查容量
title: SampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 第 5.1 节需要的是疾病阳性病例，而医院最初接触的是尚未确诊的受检者。先确定 196 例可评价确诊病例的目标，再依据拟入组门诊的患病率估计总检查容量；患病率应来自同样转诊条件下的连续病例登记。 下表比较 10%、20%、30% 患病率时的平均换算与 90% 病例数量保障。它把“估计敏感度的 95% 置信水平”和“得到足够病例的 90% 概率”分开，二者服务于不同的规划问题。 这些人数对应完成待评价检测和参考标准的受检者。临床流程还需确定谁承担参考检查、无效标本如何补采、每月能完成多少套检查；如果只有约 95% 的预约者完成两项检查，单纯把表中人数当作邀请人数并不能保留原来的病例数量保障。
code: diag_plan <- data.frame(prevalence = c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30)) diag_plan$expected <- ceiling(   res_5_1$target_state_cases_needed / diag_plan$prevalence ) diag_plan$guaranteed <- vapply(diag_plan$prevalence, function(prev) {   screen_required(res_5_1$target_state_cases_needed, prev, beta = 0.10) }, numeric(1)) knitr::kable(diag_plan,   col.names = c("门诊患病率", "按期望值换算", "90% 概率保障人数") )

what: 论文与标书方法学撰写填空模板
title: SampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 默认 print() 已包含纯文本公式、LaTeX 源码、计算过程和参考文献。 调用 summary() 可进一步查看全部输入参数、设计分类及已记录的调整：
code: summary(res_1_1) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Summary #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>  #> ── Study Design #> • Type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Design: "rct" #> • Task: "test" | Outcome: "mean" #>  #> ── Parameters #> • mean1: 10 #> • mean2: 12 #> • sd: 3 #> • alpha: 0.05 #> • power: 0.8 #>  #> ── Sample Size Results #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #>  #> ── Formula #> Plain text: #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> LaTeX: #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ #>  #> ── Calculation Process #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #>  #> ── Reference #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.1 two-sample parallel design, Eq 3.11 (p. 48; the Student t refinement is Table 3.2, p. 49). #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 5.4, p. 69 (same formula with the Student t correction term). #> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

previous_headings: 第七章：结果解读、标书撰写模板与实战图表展示 > 论文与标书方法学撰写填空模板
title: SampleSizeCalc 完整使用指南：全场景临床科研样本量计算（零基础到精通）
text: 【RCT 方案填空示例】 本研究为两臂平行、双盲、随机对照试验，主要结局为基线至第 12 周的收缩压降幅。根据【填写参数来源及其人群与测量定义】，预期两组平均降幅分别为 10 和 12 mmHg，降幅合并标准差为 3 mmHg。采用双侧 α=0.05、效能 80% 的两独立样本 t 检验规划，每组需 37 名可分析患者。按 10% 的主要结局缺失预留，每组计划招募 42 人，合计 84 人。计算使用 R 包 SampleSizeCalc，公式及方法学来源详见输出报告；缺失结局和主要分析集按预先制定的统计分析计划处理。 【诊断研究方案填空示例】 本研究拟在【填写拟应用的转诊人群】中连续验证锁定阈值的检测方法，所有受检者按统一参考标准确定疾病状态。基于【填写敏感度和患病率资料来源】，预期敏感度为 85%，计划以 95% 置信区间半宽约 0.05 估计敏感度，需 196 例可评价疾病阳性病例。假设该人群患病率为 20%，为使获得足够病例的概率至少为 90%，计划完成 1061 名受检者的全套检测。该数量保障不涵盖未完成参考检查者，具体补充招募流程另行规定。

Scenario C — Diagnostic ROC-AUC validation: Evaluate frozen continuous biomarker score reference-confirmed cases clinically comparable non-cases, recruited equal numbers. patient supplies one score one reference result. Assume AUC 0.80 95% CI half-width 0.10 binormal variance model; result must met disease-status strata, overall total. Parameter roles (example, p0 unexposed incidence cohort control-group exposure case-control study) methodological hints included available. See reporting guide field extraction rendered formula example.
code: calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.1 two-sample parallel design, Eq 3.11 (p. 48; the Student t refinement is Table 3.2, p. 49). #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 5.4, p. 69 (same formula with the Student t correction term). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> calculate("cohort", "test", "proportion", p0 = 0.20, p1 = 0.30, dropout = 0.10) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Cohort study (cumulative incidence, RR)" #> • Sample size per group: 327 #> • Exposed group: 327 #> • Unexposed group: 327 #> • Total sample size: 654 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • p0 = unexposed-group cumulative incidence #> • p1 = exposed-group cumulative incidence #> • ratio = unexposed:exposed allocation (m) #> • effect measure: risk ratio RR (estimable in cohort designs) #> Formula (plain text): #> `n1 = [Za*sqrt((1+1/m)*pbar*(1-pbar)) + Zb*sqrt(p1q1+p0q0/m)]^2/(p1-p0)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{1} = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1+\frac{1}{m})\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1)+\frac{p_0(1-p_0)}{m}}\right]^2}{(p_1-p_0)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify proportions: unexposed p0 = 0.20, exposed p1 = 0.30, #> allocation ratio m = 1 (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Weighted average proportion: p_bar = (p1 + m*p0) / (1 + m) = 0.25. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Calculate exposed sample size: n_exposed = #> [Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt((1+1/m)*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_beta*sqrt(p1*q1 + p0*q0/m)]^2 / #> (p1 - p0)^2 = 293.15. #> • Step 5: Calculate unexposed sample size: n_unexposed = m * n_exposed = 1 * #> 293.15 = 293.15. #> • Step 6: Round up before dropout inflation: ceiling(n_exposed) = 294, #> ceiling(m*n_exposed) = 294; apply dropout d = 0.10 using ceiling(n/(1-d)). #> Exposed = 327, Unexposed = 327, Total sample size N = 654. #> Reference: #> Primary: Bhardwaj et al. (2024). Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care, 13(7), 2559 (worked example: p0=0.20, p1=0.30, m=1 -> 293/group). #>  #>  Also: Schlesselman, J. J. (1982). Case-Control Studies. Oxford University Press (cohort/case-control shared formula, roles swapped); Machin et al. (2018) Ch.3. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> calculate("diagAUC", "estimate", "auc",   auc = 0.80, d = 0.10,   ratio = 1, var_method = "binormal" ) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Single-group AUC CI precision" #> • Cases needed: 46 #> • Controls needed: 46 #> • Total subjects: 92 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • auc = anticipated area under the ROC curve #> • precision = desired CI half-width L #> • ratio = controls per case (non-cases:cases; default 1) #> • prevalence = clinical disease proportion; alternative to fixed ratio #> • screening totals, when present, meet expected case and control quotas, not an #> assurance probability #> • var_method = binormal variance function #> Formula (plain text): #> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2 / d)^2 * V(AUC); controls = ceiling(ceiling(N_cases)*R), R #> = controls/cases` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{cases} = \left(\frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}}{d}\right)^2 \cdot V(AUC), \quad R = n_{controls}/n_{cases}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Anticipated AUC = 0.80, precision d = 0.10, controls:cases R = 1, #> alpha = 0.05. #> • Step 2: Use the binormal variance model: V(AUC) = 0.1195. #> • Step 3: Calculate cases: n_cases = (Z_(1-alpha/2)/d)^2 * V(AUC) = #> (1.96/0.10)^2 * 0.1195 = 45.89. #> • Step 4: Round cases up first: Target cases needed = 46; controls = #> ceiling(cases*R) = 46. #> • Step 5: Sum integer quotas: Total subjects = 46 + 46 = 92. #> Reference: #> Primary: Zhou, X.-H., Obuchowski, N. A., & McClish, D. K. (2011). Statistical Methods in Diagnostic Medicine (2nd ed.). Wiley. Section 6.1.2, pp. 196-199 (Eq 6.4/6.5/6.6; CTC worked example). #>  #>  Original variance: Hanley, J. A., & McNeil, B. J. (1982). Radiology, 143(1), 29-36. #>  Binormal variance: Obuchowski, N. A. (1994). Computing sample size for receiver operating characteristic studies. Investigative Radiology, 29(2), 238-243. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Comparing means two independent groups (e.g., treatment vs. control) Example: blinded outpatient trial compares baseline--week-12 systolic BP reductions two add-treatments. Assume group means 10 12 mmHg common change-score SD 3 mmHg. two independent groups need complete patient-level change scores; repeated BP readings averaged within visit separate patients. Interpretation: - Need 37 subjects per group - Total sample size: 74 subjects - effect size (Cohen’s d): 0.67 Formula: \[n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2\] Reference: Chow et al. (2017). Sample Size Calculations Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "twoMeans",   mean1 = 10, # Control group mean (mmHg reduction)   mean2 = 12, # Treatment group mean (mmHg reduction)   sd = 3, # Common standard deviation   alpha = 0.05, # Significance level   power = 0.8 # Target power (80%) )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.1 two-sample parallel design, Eq 3.11 (p. 48; the Student t refinement is Table 3.2, p. 49). #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Comparing means paired matched observations (e.g., pre-post measurements, matched pairs) Example: cognitive rehabilitation cohort receives prespecified cognitive assessment 12 weeks training. Assume average 2.5-point change SD patient-level differences 4.0 points, targeting 90% power. visits must linked; practice effects natural history require consideration interpreting uncontrolled change. Interpretation: - Need 29 pairs (.e., 29 measurements 29 subjects) - Standardized effect size: 0.62 Reference: Rosner (2015). Fundamentals Biostatistics (8th ed.). Cengage Learning.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "pairedMeans",   meanDiff = 2.5, # Mean difference (post-pre)   sdDiff = 4.0, # SD of differences   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.9 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Paired means" #> • Total sample size: 29 #> • Pairs needed: 29 #> • Measurements required: 58 #> • Total individuals: 29 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = ((Z_a/2 + Z_b) * sd_diff / mean_diff)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma_d}{\mu_d}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State paired difference hypotheses: H0: mu_d = 0 vs H1: mu_d != 0 #> (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.90). #> • Step 2: Expected paired difference mu_d = 2.50, SD of differences sigma_d = #> 4. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 1.2816. #> • Step 4: Normal approximation: n0 = ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma_d / #> mu_d)^2 = ((1.96 + 1.2816) * 4 / 2.50)^2 = 26.90. #> • Step 5: Exact paired Student's t-test degrees of freedom iteration. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 29 pairs (total individuals = 29). #> Reference: #> Rosner, B. (2015). *Fundamentals of biostatistics* (8th ed.). Cengage Learning. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

previous_headings: Categorical Outcomes
title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Comparing proportions two independent groups Example: exploratory oncology trial compares objective response fixed week-12 assessment, using imaging criteria randomized groups. Assume response rates 30% 45%, two-sided α=0.05 80% power. Prespecify early deaths, rescue therapy, unevaluable imaging rather excluding unsuccessful patients denominator. Interpretation: - Need 163 patients per group - Absolute risk reduction: 0.15 - Relative risk increase: 50% Reference: Fleiss et al. (2003). Statistical Methods Rates Proportions (3rd ed.). Wiley.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "twoProportions",   p1 = 0.30, # Control response rate   p2 = 0.45, # Treatment response rate   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.8 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent proportions" #> • Sample size per group: 163 #> • Total sample size: 326 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = (Z_a/2 * sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_b * sqrt(p1*(1-p1)+p2*(1-p2)))^2 / #> (p1-p2)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{2\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1) + p_2(1-p_2)}\right]^2}{(p_1 - p_2)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: p1 = p2 vs H1: p1 != p2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute pooled proportion: p_bar = (p1 + p2) / 2 = (0.30 + 0.45) / 2 #> = 0.375. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute Fleiss formula numerator components: #> Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) = 1.3419; Z_beta*sqrt(p1(1-p1)+p2(1-p2)) = #> 0.5693. #> • Step 5: Calculate unrounded sample size per group: n = (1.3419 + 0.5693)^2 / #> (0.30 - 0.45)^2 = 162.33. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 163 per group, total sample size N = 326. #> Reference: #> Primary (formula as implemented, without continuity correction): Fleiss, J. L., Tytun, A., & Ury, H. K. (1980). A simple approximation for calculating sample sizes for comparing independent proportions. Biometrics, 36(2), 343-346. #>  #> With continuity correction: Casagrande, J. T., Pike, M. C., & Smith, P. G. (1978). An improved approximate formula for calculating sample sizes for comparing two binomial distributions. Biometrics, 34(3), 483-494. #>  #> Book: Fleiss, J. L., Levin, B., & Paik, M. C. (2003). Statistical methods for rates and proportions (3rd ed.). Wiley. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

previous_headings: Survival Analysis
title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Time--event analysis log-rank test Example: randomized oncology trial uses -cause death randomization overall-survival endpoint, last-known survival censoring date. Assume HR 0.70 proportional hazards 1:1 allocation. First calculate deaths required, use accrual survival assumptions estimate patient enrollment follow-duration. Important Notes: - calculates number events needed, total sample size - Total sample size = events / event rate - example, event rate 50%, total sample size needed: 494 subjects Formula: \[E = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta})^2}{p_E(1-p_E)[\ln(HR)]^2}\] Reference: Schoenfeld (1983). Sample-size formula proportional-hazards regression model. Biometrics, 39(2), 499-503.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "survival",   hr = 0.70, # Hazard ratio (treatment vs. control)   pE = 0.50, # Proportion in experimental group (1:1 randomization)   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.8 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Survival (log-rank)" #> • Events needed: 247 #> Formula (plain text): #> `E = (Z_a/2 + Z_b)^2 / (pE*(1-pE)*log(HR)^2)` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$E = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta})^2}{p_E(1-p_E)[\ln(HR)]^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State survival parameters: Hazard Ratio HR = 0.70, experimental arm #> allocation pE = 0.50 (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute log hazard ratio: ln(HR) = ln(0.70) = -0.3567. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Apply Schoenfeld formula: E = (Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta)^2 / [pE * (1 - #> pE) * (ln HR)^2] = (1.96 + 0.8416)^2 / [0.50 * 0.50 * (-0.3567)^2] = 246.79. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target events needed E = 247. #> Reference: #> Primary: Schoenfeld, D. A. (1983). Sample-size formula for the proportional-hazards regression model. Biometrics, 39(2), 499-503. #>  #> Extensions: #> - Hsieh, F. Y., & Lavori, P. W. (2000). Sample-size calculations for the Cox proportional hazards regression model with nonbinary covariates. Controlled Clinical Trials, 21(6), 552-560. #> - Rubinstein, L. V., Gail, M. H., & Santner, T. J. (1981). Planning the duration of a comparative clinical trial with loss to follow-up and a period of continued observation. Journal of Chronic Diseases, 34(9-10), 469-479. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

previous_headings: Non-Inferiority, Superiority, and Equivalence
title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Demonstrating new treatment worse standard margin Example: parallel trial evaluates whether simpler symptom-management strategy preserves active comparator’s improvement prespecified depression score week 12. Assume mean improvements 8.0 versus 8.5 points, SD 2.0, maximum acceptable loss 1.0 point. Use one-sided α=0.025 90% power; margin needs clinical effect-preservation justification. Key Points: - Uses one-sided α (typically 0.025) - Margin Δ defines clinically acceptable difference - New treatment must within Δ standard Reference: Chow et al. (2017). Sample Size Calculations Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "nonInferiorityMeans",   mean1 = 8.0, # New treatment mean   mean2 = 8.5, # Standard treatment mean   sd = 2.0, # Common SD   margin = 1.0, # Non-inferiority margin (Δ)   alpha = 0.025, # One-sided test   power = 0.9 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Non-inferiority (means)" #> • Sample size per group: 337 #> • Total sample size: 674 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2*(Z_a+Z_b)^2*sd^2/(mean1-mean2+margin)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 + \Delta}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State non-inferiority hypotheses: H0: mu1 - mu2 <= -margin vs H1: mu1 #> - mu2 > -margin (margin Delta = 1, one-sided alpha = 0.025, power = 0.90). #> • Step 2: Effective difference: delta_E = mu1 - mu2 + margin = 8 - 8.50 + 1 = #> 0.50; SD sigma = 2. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.96, Z_beta = 1.2816. #> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = 2 * (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * sigma^2 / #> delta_E^2 = 2 * (1.96 + 1.2816)^2 * 2^2 / (0.50)^2 = 336.24. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 337 per group, total sample size N = 674. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.2 noninferiority, Eq 3.12, p. 50. #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 11.3, p. 173. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

previous_headings: Non-Inferiority, Superiority, and Equivalence
title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Demonstrating new treatment better standard Example: pain trial compares week-12 improvement specified 0–100 scale, assuming means 12 10 points SD 2.5. objective exceed active comparator 0.5 point, using one-sided α=0.025 85% power. effective difference formula anticipated difference minus prespecified superiority margin. Key Points: - Uses one-sided α - Effect must exceed margin meaningful - Smaller margin requires larger sample size
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "superiorityMeans",   mean1 = 12.0, # New treatment mean (better)   mean2 = 10.0, # Standard treatment mean   sd = 2.5, # Common SD   margin = 0.5, # Minimal clinically important difference   alpha = 0.025, # One-sided test   power = 0.85 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Superiority (means)" #> • Sample size per group: 50 #> • Total sample size: 100 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2*(Z_a+Z_b)^2*sd^2/(mean1-mean2-margin)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 - \Delta}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State superiority hypotheses: H0: mu1 - mu2 <= margin vs H1: mu1 - #> mu2 > margin (margin Delta = 0.50, one-sided alpha = 0.025, power = 0.85). #> • Step 2: Effective difference: delta_E = mu1 - mu2 - margin = 12 - 10 - 0.50 = #> 1.50; SD sigma = 2.50. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.96, Z_beta = 1.0364. #> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = 2 * (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * sigma^2 / #> delta_E^2 = 2 * (1.96 + 1.0364)^2 * 2.50^2 / (1.50)^2 = 49.88. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 50 per group, total sample size N = 100. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.2 superiority, Eq 3.12, p. 50. #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 11.3, p. 173. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

previous_headings: Non-Inferiority, Superiority, and Equivalence
title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Demonstrating two treatments equivalent Example: Two randomized anemia-support strategies compared mean hemoglobin week 12, assuming 100 versus 102 g/L SD 5 g/L. teaching equivalence interval ±5 g/L, one-sided α=0.05 80% power. equivalence specified continuous endpoint, distinct pharmacokinetic bioequivalence study. Key Points: - Uses TOST (Two One-Sided Tests) procedure - Requires Zβ/2 (larger sample size) - Margin must larger observed difference
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "equivalenceMeans",   mean1 = 100, # Test mean   mean2 = 102, # Reference mean   sd = 5, # Common SD   margin = 5, # Equivalence margin (±5 units)   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.8 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Equivalence (means)" #> • Sample size per group: 48 #> • Total sample size: 96 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2*(Z_a+Z_b/2)^2*sd^2/(margin-|mean1-mean2|)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta/2})\sigma}{\Delta - |\mu_1 - \mu_2|}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State equivalence hypotheses (TOST): H0: |mu1 - mu2| >= margin vs H1: #> |mu1 - mu2| < margin (margin Delta = 5, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Margin clearance: Delta - |mu1 - mu2| = 5 - |100 - 102| = 3; SD sigma #> = 5. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.6449, Z_(beta/2) = #> 1.2816. #> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = 2 * (Z_alpha + Z_(beta/2))^2 * sigma^2 / #> (Delta - |mu1 - mu2|)^2 = 2 * (1.6449 + 1.2816)^2 * 5^2 / (3)^2 = 47.58. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 48 per group, total sample size N = 96. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.3 equivalence, Eq 3.13, p. 51; the Z_{beta/2} convention is discussed in Section 3.6.1 (p. 67). #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 11.5-11.6, p. 174. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

previous_headings: Diagnostic Accuracy Studies
title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Estimating sensitivity specificity given precision Example: referral clinic consecutively validates locked-threshold diagnostic test using common reference examination patients. Assume sensitivity 85%, 95% CI half-width 0.05, source prevalence 20%. case requirement confirmed disease-positive patients; total screening expectation-based conversion, specificity precision requires separate planning. Interpretation: - Target state cases needed: 196 - Total subjects screen: 980 - 20% prevalence, need screen 980 get 196 cases Formula: \[n_{cases} = \frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}\] Reference: Hajian-Tilaki (2014). Sample size determination diagnostic test studies. Journal Biomedical Informatics, 48, 193-204.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "diagnosticAccuracySingle",   prob = 0.85, # Expected sensitivity   d = 0.05, # Desired precision (±5%)   prevalence = 0.20, # Disease prevalence   alpha = 0.05 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Diagnostic accuracy (single)" #> • Cases needed: 196 #> • Total subjects to screen: 980 #> Formula (plain text): #> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2)^2 * P*(1-P)/d^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{{{cases}}} = \frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify diagnostic accuracy prob (Se or Sp) = 0.85, margin of error d #> = 0.05, prevalence = 0.20 (alpha = 0.05). #> • Step 2: Determine critical value: Z_(1-alpha/2) = 1.96 (confidence level = #> 95%). #> • Step 3: Calculate target cases required: n_cases = Z_sum^2 * prob * (1 - #> prob) / d^2 = (1.96)^2 * 0.85 * 0.15 / (0.05)^2 = 195.91. #> • Step 4: Adjust for disease prevalence: total subjects to screen = n_cases / #> prevalence = 195.91 / 0.20 = 979.57. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target cases needed = 196, Total subjects to #> screen = 980. #> Reference: #> Primary: Hanley, J. A., & McNeil, B. J. (1982). The meaning and use of the area under a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Radiology, 143(1), 29-36. #>  #> Review: Hajian-Tilaki, K. (2014). Sample size estimation in diagnostic test studies of biomedical informatics. Journal of Biomedical Informatics, 48, 193-204. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Estimating AUC confidence interval given width Example: biomarker score frozen clinical validation cohort enrolled. Assume AUC 0.80, CI half-width 0.05, source prevalence 30%, one score reference disease assessment per person. branch uses binormal AUC variance model default, controls:cases allocation derived prevalence. three-axis example shows fixed case-control quotas; var_method can select alternative variance model. Key Points: - Calculates required number cases; non-case quota follows controls:cases ratio - AUC variance uses binormal model (Obuchowski 1994) default; var_method selects exponential distribution-free alternative - Screening volume requires prevalence; fixed case-control quotas report case, control, total counts instead Reference: Hanley & McNeil (1982). meaning use AUC. Radiology, 143(1), 29-36.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "auc_single",   auc = 0.80, # Expected AUC   d = 0.05, # Half-width of CI (±0.10 total)   prevalence = 0.30,   alpha = 0.05 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Single-group AUC CI precision" #> • Cases needed: 144 #> • Total subjects to screen: 480 #> • Controls needed: 336 #> • Total subjects: 480 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • auc = anticipated area under the ROC curve #> • precision = desired CI half-width L #> • ratio = controls per case (non-cases:cases; default 1) #> • prevalence = clinical disease proportion; alternative to fixed ratio #> • screening totals, when present, meet expected case and control quotas, not an #> assurance probability #> • var_method = binormal variance function #> Formula (plain text): #> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2 / d)^2 * V(AUC); controls = ceiling(ceiling(N_cases)*R), R #> = controls/cases` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{cases} = \left(\frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}}{d}\right)^2 \cdot V(AUC), \quad R = n_{controls}/n_{cases}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Anticipated AUC = 0.80, precision d = 0.05, controls:cases R = #> 2.3333, alpha = 0.05. #> • Step 2: Use the binormal variance model: V(AUC) = 0.0932. #> • Step 3: Calculate cases: n_cases = (Z_(1-alpha/2)/d)^2 * V(AUC) = #> (1.96/0.05)^2 * 0.0932 = 143.24. #> • Step 4: Round cases up first: Target cases needed = 144; controls = #> ceiling(cases*R) = 336. #> • Step 5: Sum integer quotas: Total subjects = 144 + 336 = 480. #> • Step 6: At prevalence = 0.30, meet both quotas in expectation: Total subjects #> to screen = 480. This is not an assurance probability. #> Reference: #> Primary: Zhou, X.-H., Obuchowski, N. A., & McClish, D. K. (2011). Statistical Methods in Diagnostic Medicine (2nd ed.). Wiley. Section 6.1.2, pp. 196-199 (Eq 6.4/6.5/6.6; CTC worked example). #>  #>  Original variance: Hanley, J. A., & McNeil, B. J. (1982). Radiology, 143(1), 29-36. #>  Binormal variance: Obuchowski, N. A. (1994). Computing sample size for receiver operating characteristic studies. Investigative Radiology, 29(2), 238-243. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

text: Use case: Comparing AUCs two diagnostic tests applied subjects Example: patients receive two continuous imaging scores, evaluated one common disease reference. Assume AUCs 0.85 0.80, correlation AUC estimators 0.6, prevalence 25%. Preserve pairing use pilot covariance information; correlation raw image scores automatically required AUC correlation. Key Points: - Requires correlation coefficient (r) - Higher correlation → smaller sample size - Uses Hanley-McNeil method paired design
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "aucComparison",   auc1 = 0.85, # Test 1 AUC   auc2 = 0.80, # Test 2 AUC   r = 0.6, # Correlation between AUCs   prevalence = 0.25,   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.8 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "AUC comparison (two tests)" #> • Cases needed: 208 #> • Total subjects to screen: 832 #> • Controls needed: 624 #> • Total subjects: 832 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • ratio = controls per case; prevalence is an alternative clinical recruitment #> assumption #> Formula (plain text): #> `n_cases = 2 * (Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta)^2 * V(AUC) * (1 - r) / (AUC1 - AUC2)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{cases} = \frac{2(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta})^2 \cdot V(AUC) \cdot (1-r)}{(AUC_1 - AUC_2)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Compare AUC1 = 0.85 and AUC2 = 0.80, correlation r = 0.60, #> controls:cases R = 3. #> • Step 2: Use Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 and Z_beta = 0.8416 with binormal variance. #> • Step 3: n_cases = 2*(Z_(alpha/2)+Z_beta)^2*V(AUC)*(1-r)/(AUC1-AUC2)^2 = #> 207.48. #> • Step 4: Round cases up first: Target cases needed = 208; controls = #> ceiling(cases*R) = 624. #> • Step 5: Sum integer quotas: Total subjects = 208 + 624 = 832. #> • Step 6: At prevalence = 0.25, meet both quotas in expectation: Total subjects #> to screen = 832. This is not an assurance probability. #> Reference: #> Primary: Hajian-Tilaki, K. (2014). Sample size estimation in diagnostic test studies of biomedical informatics. Journal of Biomedical Informatics, 48, 193-204 (Eq 7.6-7.8, paired/independent two-AUC comparison; the worked example on p. 199 gives n = 211 with the binormal variance). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbi.2014.02.013 #>  #>  Variance function: Zhou, X.-H., Obuchowski, N. A., & McClish, D. K. (2011). Statistical Methods in Diagnostic Medicine (2nd ed.), Eq 6.5. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

previous_headings: Case-Control Studies
title: Comprehensive Guide to SampleSizeCalc
text: Use case: Sample size case-control studies odds ratio Example: Incident lung cancer cases controls source population report smoking common index-date window. Assume 30% control exposure 2.5, one control per case. unmatched group-ratio design; p0 exposure prevalence among controls, individual age matching require different calculation. Interpretation: - Cases needed: 80 - Controls needed: 80 - Total subjects: 160 Reference: Schlesselman (1982). Case-Control Studies: Design, Conduct, Analysis. Oxford University Press.
code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   design = "caseControl",   p0 = 0.30, # Exposure rate in controls   OR = 2.5, # Target odds ratio   m = 1, # Controls per case (unmatched group ratio)   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.8 )  print(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Case-control" #> • Cases needed: 80 #> • Controls needed: 80 #> • Total subjects: 160 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n_cases = [Z_alpha/2 * sqrt((1+1/m)*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_beta * sqrt(p1*(1-p1) #> + p0*(1-p0)/m)]^2 / (p1 - p0)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{cases} = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1+1/m)\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1) + p_0(1-p_0)/m}\right]^2}{(p_1-p_0)^2}$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Compute case exposure rate from Odds Ratio: p1 = (OR * p0) / (1 - p0 #> + OR * p0) = (2.50 * 0.30) / (1 - 0.30 + 2.50 * 0.30) = 0.5172. #> • Step 2: Weighted average exposure (matching ratio m = 1): p_bar = (p1 + m*p0) #> / (1 + m) = 0.4086. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Schlesselman formula for cases: n_cases = #> [Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt((1+1/m)*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_beta*sqrt(p1*(1-p1) + #> p0*(1-p0)/m)]^2 / (p1 - p0)^2 = 79.19. #> • Step 5: Calculate controls needed: n_controls = m * n_cases = 1 * 79.19 = #> 79.19. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: Cases needed = 80, Controls needed = 80, Total #> subjects = 160. #> Reference: #> Primary: Schlesselman, J. J. (1982). Case-control studies: Design, conduct, analysis. Oxford University Press. #>  #> IARC classic: Breslow, N. E., & Day, N. E. (1980). Statistical methods in cancer research: Volume I - The analysis of case-control studies. IARC Scientific Publications No. 32. #>  #> For individually matched designs (not the formula implemented here): Dupont, W. D. (1988). Power calculations for matched case-control studies. Biometrics, 44(4), 1157-1168; see the caseControlMatched design. #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

code: result <- sample_size_calculator(   "survival",   hr = 0.70,   alpha = 0.05,   power = 0.8 )  summary(result) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Summary #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>  #> ── Study Design #> • Type: "Survival (log-rank)" #>  #> ── Parameters #> • hazard_ratio: 0.7 #> • allocation_ratio: 0.5 #> • alpha: 0.05 #> • power: 0.8 #>  #> ── Sample Size Results #> • Events needed: 247 #>  #> ── Formula #> Plain text: #> `E = (Z_a/2 + Z_b)^2 / (pE*(1-pE)*log(HR)^2)` #> LaTeX: #> $$E = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta})^2}{p_E(1-p_E)[\ln(HR)]^2}$$ #>  #> ── Calculation Process #> • Step 1: State survival parameters: Hazard Ratio HR = 0.70, experimental arm #> allocation pE = 0.50 (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute log hazard ratio: ln(HR) = ln(0.70) = -0.3567. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Apply Schoenfeld formula: E = (Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta)^2 / [pE * (1 - #> pE) * (ln HR)^2] = (1.96 + 0.8416)^2 / [0.50 * 0.50 * (-0.3567)^2] = 246.79. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target events needed E = 247. #>  #> ── Reference #> Primary: Schoenfeld, D. A. (1983). Sample-size formula for the proportional-hazards regression model. Biometrics, 39(2), 499-503. #>  #> Extensions: #> - Hsieh, F. Y., & Lavori, P. W. (2000). Sample-size calculations for the Cox proportional hazards regression model with nonbinary covariates. Controlled Clinical Trials, 21(6), 552-560. #> - Rubinstein, L. V., Gail, M. H., & Santner, T. J. (1981). Planning the duration of a comparative clinical trial with loss to follow-up and a period of continued observation. Journal of Chronic Diseases, 34(9-10), 469-479. #> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

title: Formulas, calculation steps, and references / 公式、计算过程与参考文献
text: calculate() sample_size_calculator() return sample_size_result object. Printing displays study design, required sample size, four report components. Assigning result variable stores ; print(res) entering res R console displays report. calculate() 和 sample_size_calculator() 返回 sample_size_result 对象。 默认打印会显示研究设计、所需样本量，以及以下四项内容。赋值仅保存结果； 输入对象名称或调用 print(res) 即可查看完整输出。 following example runs page built. calculation process shows normal approximation 35.32 per arm, followed noncentral t power calculation rounding 37 per arm (74 total). Intermediate calculations rounding depend chosen method. 以下示例在构建页面时实际运行。计算过程先列出每组约 35.32 人的正态近似， 再说明非中心 t 分布效能求解和取整，最终为每组 37 人、合计 74 人。 不同设计采用的中间计算与取整规则有所不同。
code: res <- calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3) print(res) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.1 two-sample parallel design, Eq 3.11 (p. 48; the Student t refinement is Table 3.2, p. 49). #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 5.4, p. 69 (same formula with the Student t correction term). #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

Statistical Methods Diagnostic Medicine (2nd ed.), Wiley - diagnostic module. Machin, Campbell, Tan & Tan (2018). Sample Sizes Clinical, Laboratory Epidemiology Studies (4th ed.), Wiley - trial/complex designs. Hajian-Tilaki (2014). J Biomed Informatics 48:193-204 - diagnostic formulas. Akoglu (2022). Turkish J Emergency Medicine 22(4):177-185 - diagnostic comparisons dual-endpoint strategy. Bhardwaj et al. (2024). J Family Med Prim Care 13(7):2555-2561 - prevalence studies dropout adjustment. Plus original methods: Schoenfeld (1983), Fleiss et al. (1980), Casagrande et al. (1978), Schlesselman (1982), Dupont (1988), Connor (1987), Hanley & McNeil (1982/1983), Buderer (1996), Simon (1989), ’Hern (2001), Whitehead (1993), Peduzzi et al. (1996), Schuirmann (1987).

title: Unified sample size calculator (three-axis API) — calculate
text: ... ... Control design arguments, resolved EXACT name (partial matching deliberately avoided design-specific arguments d swallowed design slot).
code: **Control arguments**  * `design` (first positional argument): one of `"rct"`, `"paired"`,   `"rctSingleArm"`, `"crossover"`, `"bioequivalence"`,   `"singleArmPhaseII"`, `"cohort"`, `"caseControl"`,   `"caseControlMatched"`, `"crosstab"`, `"singleProportion"`,   `"singleMean"`, `"singleCorrelation"`, `"diagAccuracy"`,   `"diagAccuracyCompare"`, `"diagAUC"`, `"diagAUCCompare"`, `"diagLR"`,   `"clusterRCT"`, `"steppedWedge"`, `"twoOrdinal"`, `"predictiveModel"`,   `"kappa"`, `"its"` - the study-design axis. * `task` (second positional argument): `"test"`, `"estimate"`,   `"noninferiority"`, `"superiority"`, `"equivalence"`, or `"plan"`;   optional for unambiguous designs. * `outcome` (third positional argument): `"mean"`, `"proportion"`,   `"rate"`, `"survival"`, `"auc"`, `"lr"`, `"correlation"`, `"ordinal"`,   or `"events"`; optional for unambiguous designs. * `alpha`: scalar in (0, 1), default 0.05. Use 0.025 for one-sided   non-inferiority trials spending a full two-sided 0.05. * `power`: scalar in (0, 1), default 0.8 (80 percent); 0.9 for   confirmatory trials. * `alternative`: `"one.sided"` (the package's historical default and the   Akoglu 2022 Table 2 Eq 2 convention) or `"two.sided"` (Hajian-Tilaki   2014 Eq 6.8 convention), or `NULL` to keep the design default.   Currently consumed by `diagAccuracy` + `test` + `proportion` only;   Supplying it for an unsupported design raises an error. * `dropout`: anticipated dropout/non-response proportion in [0, 1),   inflating by 1/(1-d). Currently applied by `cohort` + `test` +   `proportion` only; supplying it elsewhere raises an error.   Unknown or unused design-specific arguments also raise an error.  **Design-specific parameters** (all validated; ranges shown):  * *RCT, test, mean*: `mean1`, `mean2` real-valued group means (e.g.   mmHg); `sd` > 0 pooled standard deviation. * *RCT, test, proportion*: `p1`, `p2` in (0, 1) response rates, must   differ. * *RCT, test, survival*: `hr` in (0, 1) anticipated hazard ratio   (<1 = benefit); `pE` in (0, 1) experimental-arm share (default 0.5).   Returns **events** required. * *RCT, noninferiority/superiority, mean or proportion*: same inputs as   above plus `margin` > 0 (NI margin Delta, one-sided alpha; or the   minimal clinically important difference for superiority). * *RCT, equivalence, mean or proportion*: `margin` = corridor   half-width; must exceed |mean1 - mean2| (or |p1 - p2|); uses   Z_(beta/2). * *paired*: optional `pairing = "within_subject"` (default) counts   one distinct person per complete pair of observations;   `"matched_subjects"` counts two distinct people per pair.   `n_measurements` always counts two observations per pair. * *paired, mean*: `meanDiff` != 0 within-subject mean difference;   `sdDiff` > 0 SD of the differences (NOT the pooled SD). * *paired, proportion*: `p1`, `p2` in (0, 1); `psi` in (0, 1) expected   discordant-pair proportion, psi >= |p1-p2|; output in pairs. * *rctSingleArm, mean*: `mu0` historical mean, `mu1` anticipated mean,   `sigma` > 0. * *rctSingleArm, proportion*: `p0` historical rate, `p1` anticipated   rate, both in (0, 1). * *crossover, mean*: `delta` > 0 treatment difference; `sigma_within` > 0   within-subject SD. * *bioequivalence*: `cv` in (0, 1) intra-subject CV; `theta0` GMR inside   the acceptance range (default 1.0); `margin_low`/`margin_high` default   0.8/1.25 (80-125 rule). * *singleArmPhaseII*: `p0` unacceptable rate; `p1` > p0 target rate;   `optimizer` = "optimal" or "minimax". * *cohort, proportion*: `p0`, `p1` in (0, 1); `ratio` >= 1   unexposed:exposed; optional `dropout` in [0, 1) inflates by 1/(1-d). * *cohort, rate*: `rate0`, `rate1` > 0 events per person-time; `ratio`   at least  1 person-time ratio. * *caseControl*: `p0` in (0, 1) control exposure rate; `OR` > 0, != 1;   `m` >= 1 controls per case (default 1). * *caseControlMatched*: `p0`, `OR` as above; 1:1 matching built in. * *crosstab*: `p0`, `p1` in (0, 1) prevalence in unexposed/exposed. * *singleProportion*: `p` in (0, 1); `precision` > 0; `precision_type` =   "absolute" (default) or "relative". * *singleMean*: `sigma` > 0; `precision` > 0 margin of error. * *singleCorrelation*: `r` in (0, 1); exactly one of `precision`   (absolute CI half-width in (0, 1)) or `epsilon` (relative). * *diagAccuracy, estimate*: `prob` in (0, 1) expected Se/Sp; `d` in   (0, 1) CI half-width; `prevalence` in (0, 1]; optional `ci_method` =   "precision" (Zhou Eq 6.2) or "ci_width_power" (Eq 6.1, uses `power`). * *diagAccuracy, test*: `prob`, `p0` in (0, 1); `method` = "asymptotic"   or "exact" (one-sided A'Hern; a two-sided request errors).   Dual-endpoint planning adds `prob_spec`, `p0_spec`, `dual = TRUE`,   and `dual_power` (default 0.90 per endpoint). Cases and non-cases   have separate quotas; screening is the maximum of the prevalence-   adjusted quotas in expectation. Omit prevalence for separate strata. * *diagAccuracyCompare*: `p1`, `p2` in (0, 1); `paired` = TRUE requires   `psi` in (0, 1); margin tasks add `margin` in (0, 1). * *diagAUC, estimate/test and diagAUCCompare, test*: optional `ratio` > 0   means controls per case (non-cases:cases; default 1). Alternatively,   supply `prevalence` in (0, 1) for clinical recruitment, with   R = (1-prevalence)/prevalence. Supply only one of these arguments.   `var_method` defaults to `"binormal"`; alternatives are   `"exponential"` and `"conservative"`. Fixed quotas return   `controls_needed` and `total_subjects`; `total_subjects_to_screen`   is present only for clinical recruitment and is expectation-based.   Historical `prevalence = 1` selects the default 1:1 quota. * *diagAUC, estimate*: `auc` in (0, 1); `d` > 0. * *diagAUC, test*: `auc`, `auc0` in (0, 1), auc > auc0. * *diagAUCCompare*: `auc1`, `auc2` in (0, 1); `r` in [0, 1) (default   0.5); margin tasks add `margin` in (0, 1). * *diagLR, estimate*: `sens`, `spec` in (0, 1); `lr_type` = "positive"   or "negative"; `target_lr` > 0 the boundary the CI must not cross. * *clusterRCT*: base two-group args plus `icc` in [0, 1) and   `cluster_size` integer >= 1 (DE = 1 + (m-1)*ICC). * *steppedWedge*: `theta` != 0; `tau2` > 0; `sigma2_ind` > 0; `m` >= 1;   `n_clusters` integer >= 2, a multiple of `clusters_per_step` >= 1. * *twoOrdinal*: `or` > 0, != 1; `prop_bar` positive vector summing to 1. * *predictiveModel, binary*: `prev` in (0, 1); `n_parameters` integer   at least  1; `r2_cs` within its feasible maximum; `shrinkage` default 0.9;   `mape` default 0.05; `precision_delta` default 0.05. * *predictiveModel, rate*: `rate` > 0 per person-year; `timepoint` > 0;   `precision_delta` in (0, 1); optional `n_parameters`/`epv` cross-check. * *predictiveModel, events*: `n_parameters` >= 1; `epv` >= 1 (classic   10); `event_prevalence` in (0, 1). * *predictiveModel, plan, binary*: `prev` in (0, 1), positive integer   `n_parameters`, and anticipated adjusted Cox-Snell `r2_cs` below its   prevalence-specific maximum. `shrinkage` defaults to 0.9 and must   exceed `r2_cs` and be below 1; `precision_delta` defaults to 0.05.   The returned size meets B1 (outcome precision), B3 (shrinkage), and   B4 (Nagelkerke R-squared optimism at most 0.05). `mape` defaults to   0.05 and is informational for at most 30 predictor parameters;   it does not constrain the returned size. * *kappa, estimate*: `pi1`, `pi2` in (0, 1); `kappa` in [0, 1); `d` in   (0, 1). * *kappa, test*: `kappa1` != `kappa2` in (0, 1); same pi's. * *its*: `effect_sd` > 0; `n_pre`, `n_post` integers >= 3 (>= 8   recommended); `rho` in [0, 1). Returns achieved power.

title: Unified sample size calculator (three-axis API) — calculate
text: Object class sample_size_result print, summary, plot methods. Default printing shows sample sizes, plain-text formula (formula), LaTeX source (formula_latex), calculation process (calculation_steps, also available calculation), literature references (reference). New-style objects also carry axis metadata (task, outcome, design_canonical, results, roles, adjustments). summary.sample_size_result() additionally lists input parameters recorded adjustments.

title: Unified sample size calculator (three-axis API) — calculate

# Antihypertensive RCT: placebo 10 mmHg vs new drug 12 mmHg SBP reduction, # pooled SD 3 mmHg, two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left( rac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{ eta}}{\delta}ight)^2 = 2\left( rac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{ eta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}ight)^2$$  #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.1 two-sample parallel design, Eq 3.11 (p. 48; the Student t refinement is Table 3.2, p. 49). #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 5.4, p. 69 (same formula with the Student t correction term).  #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>   # Generic vs originator antidiabetic, non-inferiority margin 1 point, # one-sided alpha 0.05 calculate(   design = "rct", task = "noninferiority", outcome = "mean",   mean1 = 10, mean2 = 9.5, sd = 3, margin = 1 ) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Non-inferiority (means)" #> • Sample size per group: 50 #> • Total sample size: 100 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2*(Z_a+Z_b)^2*sd^2/(mean1-mean2+margin)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left( rac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{ eta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 + \Delta}ight)^2$$  #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State non-inferiority hypotheses: H0: mu1 - mu2 <= -margin vs H1: mu1 #> - mu2 > -margin (margin Delta = 1, one-sided alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Effective difference: delta_E = mu1 - mu2 + margin = 10 - 9.50 + 1 = #> 1.50; SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.6449, Z_beta = #> 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = 2 * (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * sigma^2 / #> delta_E^2 = 2 * (1.6449 + 0.8416)^2 * 3^2 / (1.50)^2 = 49.46. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 50 per group, total sample size N = 100. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.2 noninferiority, Eq 3.12, p. 50. #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 11.3, p. 173.  #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>   # Bioequivalence of a generic amlodipine: intra-subject CV 25%, # expected GMR 1.0, 80-125% acceptance range (2x2 crossover) calculate("bioequivalence", cv = 0.25) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Bioequivalence (2x2 crossover, exact TOST integration)" #> • Required sample size: 12 #> • Total sample size: 24 #> • Power achieved: 0.8372 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • cv = intra-subject coefficient of variation (log scale implied) #> • theta0 = anticipated geometric mean ratio (true ratio, default 1.0) #> • margin = [0.80, 1.25] average BE criteria #> • n is per sequence; total subjects = 2n #> Formula (plain text): #> `power = E[max(0, Phi((U-mu)/SE-t*sqrt(V/df))-Phi((L-mu)/SE+t*sqrt(V/df)))], V #> ~ chi-square(df), df=N-2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$\mathrm{Power}=E\!\left[\max\!\left\{0,\Phi\!\left( rac{U-\mu}{SE}-t\sqrt{V/
u}ight)-\Phi\!\left( rac{L-\mu}{SE}+t\sqrt{V/
u}ight)ight\}ight],\quad V\sim\chi^2_
u,\ 
u=N-2$$  #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Log-scale within-subject SD = sqrt(log(1+CV^2)) = 0.246221; #> anticipated log ratio = 0.000000. #> • Step 2: TOST log limits are [-0.223144, 0.223144], each with one-sided alpha #> 0.0500. #> • Step 3: Integrate the conditional normal acceptance probability over the #> chi-square variance estimate (df = N-2); negative-width acceptance intervals #> contribute zero. #> • Step 4: Search balanced even totals for the smallest N meeting the target #> power. #> • Step 5: n = 12 per sequence, total N = 24, achieved power = 0.837226 (target #> 0.8000). #> Reference: #> Primary: Phillips, K. Tutorial in biostatistics: sample sizes for clinical trials with normal data. J Pharmacokinet Biopharm, 15(6), 657-680; #>  Chow & Liu (2009). Design and Analysis of Bioavailability and Bioequivalence Studies.  #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>   # Colorectal cancer screening kit: expected sensitivity 85%, # CI half-width +/-5%, clinic prevalence 20% calculate("diagAccuracy", "estimate", "proportion",   prob = 0.85, d = 0.05, prevalence = 0.20 ) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Diagnostic accuracy (single)" #> • Cases needed: 196 #> • Total subjects to screen: 980 #> Formula (plain text): #> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2)^2 * P*(1-P)/d^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n_{{{cases}}} =  rac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}$$  #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: Specify diagnostic accuracy prob (Se or Sp) = 0.85, margin of error d #> = 0.05, prevalence = 0.20 (alpha = 0.05). #> • Step 2: Determine critical value: Z_(1-alpha/2) = 1.96 (confidence level = #> 95%). #> • Step 3: Calculate target cases required: n_cases = Z_sum^2 * prob * (1 - #> prob) / d^2 = (1.96)^2 * 0.85 * 0.15 / (0.05)^2 = 195.91. #> • Step 4: Adjust for disease prevalence: total subjects to screen = n_cases / #> prevalence = 195.91 / 0.20 = 979.57. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target cases needed = 196, Total subjects to #> screen = 980. #> Reference: #> Primary: Hanley, J. A., & McNeil, B. J. (1982). The meaning and use of the area under a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Radiology, 143(1), 29-36. #>  #> Review: Hajian-Tilaki, K. (2014). Sample size estimation in diagnostic test studies of biomedical informatics. Journal of Biomedical Informatics, 48, 193-204.  #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>   # AUC precision for a biomarker validation cohort: AUC 0.80, # CI half-width 0.10, 1:1 case:control, binormal variance calculate("diagAUC", auc = 0.80, d = 0.05, var_method = "binormal") #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Single-group AUC CI precision" #> • Cases needed: 184 #> • Controls needed: 184 #> • Total subjects: 368 #> Parameter roles #>  #> • auc = anticipated area under the ROC curve #> • precision = desired CI half-width L #> • ratio = controls per case (non-cases:cases; default 1) #> • prevalence = clinical disease proportion; alternative to fixed ratio #> • screening totals, when present, meet expected case and control quotas, not an #> assurance probability #> • var_method = binormal variance function #> ! text: Computes power multi-reader multi-case study detect given difference accuracy (e.g. ROC area) J readers, using non-central F framework Zhou et al. (2011) Eq 6.32 Table 6.4 parameterisation paired-patient, paired-reader design (rho1 > rho2 > rho3 > 0, rho_b > 0).

title: MRMC study power (Obuchowski-Rockette mixed model, paired-patient paired-reader design) — mrmc_power
text: n Patients condition (paired-patient design: patients imaged tests) J Number readers per test; integer >= 2 (F test needs J-1 df). delta Difference accuracy detect; number > 0 (AUC accuracy metric scale, e.g. 0.10). sigma_b2 -reader variance component; number >= 0. Planning heuristic: (accuracy range / 4)^2 (Zhou p. 223, Beam 1996). sigma_w2 Within-reader (occasion) variance component; number >= 0. sigma_c2 Patient-sampling (case) variance component; number >= 0. variance accuracy estimate attributable sampling patients, .e. V()/n (Zhou p. 221), already carries sample size. mammography example 0.00196 n = 50. rho1 Correlation, reader different tests; [0, 1). rho2 Correlation, different readers test; [0, 1). rho3 Correlation, different readers different tests; [0, 1). paired-patient, paired-reader parameterisation expects rho1 > rho2 > rho3 > 0 (Zhou Table 6.4); violated orderings warn. rho_b Correlation readers' accuracies two tests (Zhou Table 6.3 p_b); [0, 1). Defaults rho1, value implied single "reader, different test" correlation supplied. Zhou mammography example book sets rho_b = 0.75. alpha Type error two-sided F test; (0, 1), default 0.05. n_repeats Reading occasions per reader-test (Q); integer >= 1, usually 1.

title: MRMC study power (Obuchowski-Rockette mixed model, paired-patient paired-reader design) — mrmc_power
text: Eq 6.32 printed (Zhou 2011, p. 221): Note two features distinguish simpler MRMC formulae: -reader term weighted (1 - rho_b), correlation readers' accuracies two tests, patient-sampling term sigma_c2 divided n (sigma_c2 already patient-sampling variance component, computed V()/n; see Zhou p. 221). Anchor: Zhou 2011 p. 225 (mammography example) - n = 50 malignant 50 benign patients, J = 8 readers, delta = 0.10, sigma_b2 = 0.00123, sigma_w2 = 0.00087, sigma_c2 = 0.00196 (Eq 6.5 n = 50), rho1 = 0.5, rho2 = 0.3, rho3 = 0.25, rho_b = 0.75 -> power = 0.893, reproduces book's "89% power".
code: lambda = J (v1 - v2)^2 / (2 * {     sigma_b2 (1 - rho_b) + sigma_w2 / Q +     sigma_c2 [(1 - rho1) + (J - 1)(rho2 - rho3)] })

code: # Antihypertensive RCT: 37 patients per arm with these assumptions res <- calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3) print(res)   # sample sizes, both formulas, calculation process, references #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$  #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.1 two-sample parallel design, Eq 3.11 (p. 48; the Student t refinement is Table 3.2, p. 49). #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 5.4, p. 69 (same formula with the Student t correction term).  #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

code: # Antihypertensive RCT: 10 vs 12 mmHg SBP reduction, SD 3 -> 37 per arm sample_size_calculator("twoMeans", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$  #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #> Reference: #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.1 two-sample parallel design, Eq 3.11 (p. 48; the Student t refinement is Table 3.2, p. 49). #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 5.4, p. 69 (same formula with the Student t correction term).  #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>   # NSCLC immunotherapy trial: HR = 0.70, 1:1 allocation -> 247 events sample_size_calculator("survival", hr = 0.7, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.8) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Survival (log-rank)" #> • Events needed: 247 #> Formula (plain text): #> `E = (Z_a/2 + Z_b)^2 / (pE*(1-pE)*log(HR)^2)` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$E = \frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta})^2}{p_E(1-p_E)[\ln(HR)]^2}$$  #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State survival parameters: Hazard Ratio HR = 0.70, experimental arm #> allocation pE = 0.50 (alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute log hazard ratio: ln(HR) = ln(0.70) = -0.3567. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Apply Schoenfeld formula: E = (Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta)^2 / [pE * (1 - #> pE) * (ln HR)^2] = (1.96 + 0.8416)^2 / [0.50 * 0.50 * (-0.3567)^2] = 246.79. #> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target events needed E = 247. #> Reference: #> Primary: Schoenfeld, D. A. (1983). Sample-size formula for the proportional-hazards regression model. Biometrics, 39(2), 499-503. #>  #> Extensions: #> - Hsieh, F. Y., & Lavori, P. W. (2000). Sample-size calculations for the Cox proportional hazards regression model with nonbinary covariates. Controlled Clinical Trials, 21(6), 552-560. #> - Rubinstein, L. V., Gail, M. H., & Santner, T. J. (1981). Planning the duration of a comparative clinical trial with loss to follow-up and a period of continued observation. Journal of Chronic Diseases, 34(9-10), 469-479.  #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>   # H. pylori eradication: quadruple 85% vs triple 70% -> 121 per arm sample_size_calculator("twoProportions", p1 = 0.85, p2 = 0.70) #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results #> • Design type: "Two independent proportions" #> • Sample size per group: 121 #> • Total sample size: 242 #> Formula (plain text): #> `n = (Z_a/2 * sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) + Z_b * sqrt(p1*(1-p1)+p2*(1-p2)))^2 / #> (p1-p2)^2` #> Formula (LaTeX): #> $$n = \frac{\left[Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{2\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})} + Z_{\beta}\sqrt{p_1(1-p_1) + p_2(1-p_2)}\right]^2}{(p_1 - p_2)^2}$$  #> Calculation process: #>  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: p1 = p2 vs H1: p1 != p2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Compute pooled proportion: p_bar = (p1 + p2) / 2 = (0.85 + 0.70) / 2 #> = 0.775. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96, Z_beta = 0.8416. #> • Step 4: Compute Fleiss formula numerator components: #> Z_(alpha/2)*sqrt(2*p_bar*(1-p_bar)) = 1.1575; Z_beta*sqrt(p1(1-p1)+p2(1-p2)) = #> 0.4889. #> • Step 5: Calculate unrounded sample size per group: n = (1.1575 + 0.4889)^2 / #> (0.85 - 0.70)^2 = 120.47. #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 121 per group, total sample size N = 242. #> Reference: #> Primary (formula as implemented, without continuity correction): Fleiss, J. L., Tytun, A., & Ury, H. K. (1980). A simple approximation for calculating sample sizes for comparing independent proportions. Biometrics, 36(2), 343-346. #>  #> With continuity correction: Casagrande, J. T., Pike, M. C., & Smith, P. G. (1978). An improved approximate formula for calculating sample sizes for comparing two binomial distributions. Biometrics, 34(3), 483-494. #>  #> Book: Fleiss, J. L., Levin, B., & Paik, M. C. (2003). Statistical methods for rates and proportions (3rd ed.). Wiley.  #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>

code: # Full protocol-ready report for the antihypertensive RCT: res <- calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3) summary(res)  # also lists all inputs, design axes, and adjustments #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Summary #> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #>  #> ── Study Design  #> • Type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison" #> • Design: "rct" #> • Task: "test" | Outcome: "mean" #>  #> ── Parameters  #> • mean1: 10 #> • mean2: 12 #> • sd: 3 #> • alpha: 0.05 #> • power: 0.8 #>  #> ── Sample Size Results  #> • Sample size per group: 37 #> • Total sample size: 74 #>  #> ── Formula  #> Plain text: #> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2` #> LaTeX: #> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$  #>  #> ── Calculation Process  #> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha = #> 0.05, power = 0.80). #> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common #> SD sigma = 3. #> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha = #> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80). #> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 * #> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 = #> 35.32. #> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration #> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2). #> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74. #>  #> ── Reference  #> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.1 two-sample parallel design, Eq 3.11 (p. 48; the Student t refinement is Table 3.2, p. 49). #>  #>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 5.4, p. 69 (same formula with the Student t correction term).  #> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
